decisive_items: a 15 cm mass possibly arising from the vaginal wall with a potential fistulous connection to the cecum
past history included a hysterectomy for micro-invasive cervical carcinoma in 2002
mesenteric lymph nodes measuring up to 27 mm but no distant metastases
response.rationale: Prior cervical cancer with vaginal wall mass and fistulization strongly favors recurrent cervical cancer over primary vaginal cancer; negative tumor markers and no distant metastases support local recurrence.

rejected.why: Carcinomatosis implies diffuse peritoneal spread, but imaging shows no distant metastases and only regional nodes.
Cecal cancer would not explain vaginal wall origin or prior cervical cancer history.
Inflammatory bowel disease lacks fistulous mass origin from vaginal wall and weight loss with elevated LDH is more neoplastic.
Primary vaginal cancer is possible but less likely given prior cervical carcinoma and hysterectomy.
Sarcoma is not supported by specific imaging features or tumor marker negativity; carcinoma more consistent.
Lymphoma would typically show more systemic features and normal WBC with negative markers is atypical; mass origin favors carcinoma.
Carcinoma is too broad; recurrent cervical cancer is the specific diagnosis.
